fixture_name: Four-lane arterial improvement — US preliminary design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Closely-spaced intersection queuing/turning/parking conflicts on a corridor with recorded high-accident designation is a genuine, scheme-specific preliminary-design safety issue affecting vehicle occupants.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal interference claim is supported by a verbatim quote from EV-US-016 matching the statement text, exceeding registry-id-only citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern under FHWA RSA preliminary-design semantics with no compliance question conflated into it.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and viable actions—turning-movement restriction and relocating named parking stalls outside the intersection functional area—are actionable at preliminary design.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly acknowledged as potentially present, but impacts are not analyzed since the mechanism is scoped to vehicle-vehicle conflicts, fitting the not-applicable-but-acknowledged case.

justifications.substance: Closely spaced signalized intersections (~650 ft apart) with queue-spillback risk on a corridor with recorded high-accident designations is a recognized, substantive preliminary-design-stage safety issue.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal 650-ft spacing claim is supported by a verbatim quoted evidence item (EV-US-001); other claims are labeled as recorded inputs (TABLE A.1 Issue 1), with no invented content detected.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Properly framed as a safety concern categorically distinct from any compliance question, consistent with FHWA RSA semantics at the preliminary design stage.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable (signal coordination, Do Not Block Intersection signs, conspicuity enhancements) and viable at preliminary design, though it does not explicitly carry forward the queue-storage check named in the statement.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly acknowledged at both signalized intersections with a reasoned scoping to vehicle occupants, but no VRU-specific impact analysis (e.g., pedestrian phasing under coordination) is offered, fitting the acknowledged-but-not-applicable tier.
